rows.english: And the same goes for every existing entity: they are nothing but a name and a concept, "This we call this, and that we call that," applied to the collection of parts that acts as the basis of the particular entity's name. There does not exist the single tiniest bit of anything that is some kind of object on its own, divorced of the parts we give its name.

rows.english: And yet there is no such problem. No matter how many arguments of this kind you want to present, they are all made from the point of view of denying the existence of external objects. The way these arguments go is as follows. If the color blue were to exist as an external object, then the following would occur when this color appeared directly to a sense perception grasping blue; that is, with such a perception found in the mental stream of one of those who "only sees this side" [which is another name for those who have not yet perceived emptiness directly]. When an earlier instance of the perception of blue ends, what actually happens is that it plants a mental seed which eventually grows into a later instance of the same perception of blue, when the seed ripens. Suppose the blue were not just this kind of appearance, but rather an appearance where blue as an outer object were transmitting a likeness of itself and thereby appearing to one's perceptions. Something else then would be happening when the three different beings sit down together and look at the glass full of something wet and flowing. The three different objects would be appearing to them because each of the objects was transmitting a likeness of itself to their perception. All of this would be happening independent of any process where each being's karma planted a mental seed, which later ripened and produced the appearance of the object.

rows.acip: KHYAB STE, RANG RKYA THUB PA'I THA DAD DU YOD NA, PHUNG PO LA MA BLTOS PAR YOD DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: khyab ste, rang rkya thub pa'i tha dad du yod na, phung po la ma bltos par yod dgos pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: I don't see that there's any necessary relationship between the two. And yet there is! Because if something were self-standing, and different from the body & mind, then it would have to exist without relying on the body & mind.

rows.acip: KHYAB STE, SNANG BA LTAR THA DAD DU GRUB NA, RANG GI GDAGS GZHI LA MA BLTOS PAR GRUB DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: khyab ste, snang ba ltar tha dad du grub na, rang gi gdags gzhi la ma bltos par grub dgos pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: I disagree that—just because something exists through relying on the thing which is given its particular name—it doesn't actually exist in the way it appears to—to the senses of a normal person—as a separate thing. And this necessarily is the case, since—if the water pitcher existed as a separate thing, as it appears to—then it would have to exist without relying on the thing which is given its particular name.

rows.english: We can, in short, say that there is no object in the universe which exists through any nature of its own—which exists in and of itself, without depending on a process where its existence is established through the application of words and mental pictures to its assembled parts.

rows.english: The reason here is that—when we speak of a “great mountain of merit”—the “mountain” implies a combination or collection of things. rows.english: If we take this latter part as referring to the inhabitants of the worlds, then the point is that the bodies of these inhabitants, these beings, are gross objects which have resulted from a collection of tiniest particles. rows.english: Here's then what the name "stage of completion" refers to.
